newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: The South African rand changed out of reverse and into a higher gear than the dollar late Tuesday after the market decided to reassess its carefully constructed long dollar positions.
"They've cut back a little, but I think the guys will stay cautiously long. It depends on how many bought into the dollar yesterday," said one dealer.
The rand pegged a closing level of 4.6650/6680 on the dollar from Monday's official close of 4.6665/6695 and well off its intraday worst of 4.6770 bid.
Dealers said Wednesday's session was likely to remain quiet with any overnight weakening by the dollar expected to be seized on at the open but without much momentum.
"I think most of the guys are looking at the gold price and the dollar. If the dollar weakens overnight we could see ourselves a fair bit stronger," a dealer said.
The rand had mixed fortunes in cross rate dealings the rand was last quoted at 0.3992/3996 on the weakened mark from 0.3979/3983 Monday and at 24.8736/9003 yen from 24.9026/9293.
Against sterling, the rand last traded at 7.3637/3731 from Monday's late level of 7.4175/4269.

After a strong start on short covering, bonds dithered over the afternoon to close off their best levels of the day, having failed to make much of lower-than-expected June producer price index (PPI) figures.
The benchmark R150 bond ended official trading at 14.105 percent from 14.115 percent just after the PPI news and Monday's close at 14.23 percent.

June's Producer Price Index was up 7.5 percent year on year or down 0.2 percent month-on-month from 8.4 and 0.9 percent in May. Economists had forecast PPI as rising 8.3 percent year-on-year or 0.5 percent month-on-month in June.
Economists said the PPI was likely continue to trend lower.
"We forecase the year-on-year PPI growth rate for July 1997 to decline further to 7.0 percent," Huysamer Stals chief economist John Rossouw said in a statement.
Barnard Jacobs Mellet economist Chantal Friedman said that the latest data meant that the average monthly increase in the first six months of the year was 0.4 percent.

"That is half of the 0.8 percent increase recorded in the second half of last year, so the trend is definitely downwards and we could well be looking at a year-end figure of six percent," Friedman said.
Players said the market remained vulnerable as it needed to consolidate the latest move lower in yields.
"Personally I think its a little overdone, There's a lot of stock coming in at the ten level," said one bond dealer.
"In my opinion its just too low. The money market still hasn't come down, it's still very tight. I think it could move back up a bit tomorrow."
In the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.40 to 15.50 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 14.90 to 14.95 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 9.602 billion rand on Monday from 8.834 billion rand on Friday.
Foreigners sold 252.53 million rands worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying a net 834.37 million rands on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
